text: Sometimes one single number matters far more than any comparison could. Here's how to show it well, and how to let viewers filter it themselves without ever opening a separate pane.

A card puts one measure front and center on the page — total sales, signups this month, whatever matters most right now. Drop a card visual on the canvas and add a measure to Values. Add more than one value, and more cards appear automatically, side by side.

A bare number rarely tells the whole story, though. Reference labels pair the headline number with supporting detail — Revenue variance and its percentage, right alongside the main figure, or Returns next to a Units count. A KPI visual goes one step further still: instead of just showing a value, it shows progress toward an actual measurable target, which matters anywhere you're tracking a quota or a goal.

Slicers put filtering right on the report canvas — always visible, unlike the Filters pane, which a viewer has to open deliberately. Power BI offers several types: the general-purpose slicer, button slicers for a more visual style, list slicers for large datasets, and input slicers for free-form text matching. And here's a subtlety worth knowing: turn on Select all, select it, then clear one value — the slicer applies an is-not filter for just that one cleared value, not an is filter listing everything else. New data added later gets included automatically, since nothing explicitly excluded it.
